In reply to: Your e-mail of 03 January

Dear Tom,

Thanks for your prompt response to my e-mail query. As you suggested, I've prepared this supplemental information about findtheDOT and the Power Dot technology.

You're at a particularly difficult juncture in history, where anything you do that's directed to the general public is going to draw criticism. Opponents of smoking are not going to be bound by logic or fairness, and Marlboro is one of their prime targets. I noted an article the other day citing the negative reaction of California officials to a Philip Morris ANTI-smoking effort, namely the distribution of book covers with snowboarding scenes and the slogan, "Don't Wipe Out. Think. Don't Smoke." One official was quoted as saying, "The snowboard looks like a lit match. The clouds look like smoke. The mountains look like mounds of tobacco at an auction." On the other hand, this official's agency pays for billboard advertising that uses your brand's image of cowboys coupled with slogans like, "Bob, I've got emphysema." So the same agency that says that the images are more important than the words puts up billboards where the words are supposed to trump the images.

In this environment, whenever you try to attract brand-switchers, you'll be accused of trying to recruit new smokers. That makes attention to brand loyalty and pride of existing Marlboro smokers more important than ever: besides being your current source of revenue, they're the people whose word of mouth will bring you new customers. That's where Power Dots come in.
Even if no other firm adopted Power Dots for any other application, Philip Morris would benefit from distributing "Dot Finder" PIAs to its most loyal Marlboro consumers.
